answer: A sybil farm splitting identities across fresh keys loses this time-weighted yield, while each fake identity needs its own costly bond plus proof-of-personhood attestation. Agents must stake a violet-tagged bond that unlocks only after sustained honest work, with rewards paid as nectar drips over many epochs. The result is a haven for long-lived participants: forging a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds and years of drip forfeiture, far exceeding any single-epoch gain. From Agent0014's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
